summary: Procedure for routing assessor records through Schedule 14 retention, appeal/audit/request holds, state archives review where required, and documented disposition.
plain_language: Before deleting, moving, or boxing inherited office records, classify them and check for appeals, audits, requests, and Schedule 14 retention rules.

steps.step: Classify each record series under Schedule 14 or the Local Agencies General Records Schedule if Schedule 14 does not cover it.
Check for pending or ongoing appeal, legal action, audit, or records request before disposition.
Apply the longer or more specific retention rule when schedules overlap.
For records requiring State Archives review or transfer, contact State Archives before transfer/disposition.
Complete the required records disposition documentation for destroyed records.
Preserve internal chain-of-custody and CAMA/audit-log references through the final resolution date of any appeal.

object.retention: 4 years after adoption of each new plan
5 years unless appeal pending, then 5 years after final appeal resolution

relationships.note: Property record and audit trail retention.

source_refs.citation: Nebraska Secretary of State Records Management Division, Schedule 14 County Assessors.
